description: We are a team of passionate CSE students participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are interested in space exploration, AI, software development, and solving real-world problems using NASA data. Our goal is to build an innovative and impactful solution through collaboration, creativity, and technology. We welcome enthusiastic teammates with skills in Python, AI/ML, web development, data analysis, UI/UX design, and space science.
summary:
EARTH-X (Planetary Analog Intelligence) is an interactive research platform developed to identify and evaluate Earth locations that can serve as analog environments for future human exploration and permanent settlements on the Moon and Mars.

The platform integrates planetary elevation data from NASA’s MOLA and LOLA datasets with Earth elevation information to explore terrain characteristics across different planetary environments. It provides automated data retrieval, interactive 3D terrain visualization, elevation mapping, geomorphometric analysis, and measurements such as relief, slope and surface roughness.

EARTH-X examines potential terrestrial analog locations, including the Atacama Desert, Ladakh, Namib Desert, Antarctic Dry Valleys, Icelandic Highlands and Mauna Kea. Its Mission Suitability Lab provides a transparent framework for evaluating terrain and mission-planning factors, while its Scientific Evidence Ledger documents data sources, measurements and limitations.

By bringing planetary data exploration and Earth analog assessment into one accessible platform, EARTH-X aims to support scientific investigation and preliminary mission-planning research for humanity’s future beyond Earth.
details:
What is EARTH-X?

EARTH-X (Planetary Analog Intelligence) is an interactive research platform designed to explore terrestrial environments that may serve as analogs for future human exploration of Mars and the Moon.

How does it work?

EARTH-X retrieves planetary elevation datasets and Earth elevation information to investigate terrain characteristics across different environments. It provides interactive 3D terrain visualization, elevation maps, geomorphometric feature screening, and measurements including elevation, slope, surface roughness and terrain relief.

The platform explores six potential Earth analog environments: Atacama Desert, Ladakh Cold Desert, Namib Desert, Antarctic Dry Valleys, Icelandic Highlands and Mauna Kea.

Its Mission Suitability Lab provides a transparent screening framework that allows users to adjust the importance of different mission-planning factors. The Scientific Evidence Ledger helps document measurements, data sources and limitations.

Benefits and intended impact

EARTH-X makes planetary terrain exploration more accessible by bringing Earth and planetary data analysis into one interactive platform. It aims to support researchers, students and space enthusiasts in investigating terrestrial analog environments and understanding the challenges associated with future lunar and Martian exploration.

Technology used

  • Python and FastAPI for the backend.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the frontend.
  • Interactive browser-based 3D terrain visualization.
  • NASA MOLA and LOLA planetary elevation datasets.
  • Open-Meteo elevation data for Earth terrain exploration.
  • CSV-based Earth analog site information.

EARTH-X was developed as a research prototype through iterative development, testing and refinement. Scientific limitations and differences in native dataset resolution are explicitly communicated to avoid presenting exploratory results as confirmed planetary equivalence or mission certification.
